title_en: How Do We Teach Creed to the Common People and to Children?
body_ar: نفهمهم ذلك كما أفهمه الرسول (ص)، فالرسول مرسل إليهم وأتاهم وعلمهم العقيدة، فجاءه رجل وقد صف الصفوف للقتال يوم أحد، فقال له يا رسول الله، أقاتل أو أسلم؟ فقال: أسلم ثم قاتل، فقال: أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وأنك رسول الله وأخذ سيفه وقاتل حتى قتل، فقال رسول الله (ص): عمل هذا قليلا وأجر كثيرا، فلم يعرف من تفاصيل العقيدة إلا شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وأن محمدا رسول الله، ومع ذلك دخل الجنة، وحديث أبي موسى هذا في الصحيحين كما تعلمون، وكذلك فإن رسول الله (ص) لم يعلمنا كثيرا من الصفات في الملأ ولم يشرط على الناس تعلمها، بل كثير من صفات الله تعالى إنما جاءت في أخبار الآحاد فلا يجب على العوام تعلمها، إنما يجب على العوام أن يؤمنوا بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر والقدر خيره وشره فقط، أما تفاصيل ذلك فمن زاد فيها واستزاد فقد تعلم علما نافعا واكتسب أجرا ولكنه لا يجب عليه ذلك، إنما يجب هذا على أهل العلم والمشتغلين به.
body_en:
We make them understand it just as the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, made them understand it. For the Messenger was sent to them, and he came to them and taught them creed (ʿaqīdah). A man came to him when the ranks had been drawn up for battle on the day of Uhud, and said to him: Messenger of God, shall I fight, or shall I submit? He said: Submit, then fight. So he said: I bear witness that there is no god but God and that you are the Messenger of God — and he took his sword and fought until he was killed. And the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, said: 'This one worked little and was rewarded much.' He knew of the details of creed nothing but the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God, and even so he entered the Garden. And this hadith of Abu Musa is in the two Sahihs, as you know.

Likewise, the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, did not teach us many of the attributes in open assembly, and did not make the learning of them a condition upon people. Indeed many of the attributes of God, exalted, came only in singly transmitted reports (āḥād), so learning them is not obligatory upon the common people. What is obligatory upon the common people is only that they believe in God, and His angels, and His books, and His messengers, and the Last Day, and the divine decree, its good and its evil — that alone. As for the details of that: whoever adds to them and seeks more of them has learnt a beneficial knowledge and gained reward, but that is not obligatory upon him. This is obligatory only upon the people of knowledge and those occupied with it.

flags.arabic: وحديث أبي موسى هذا في الصحيحين كما تعلمون
flags.context: the Sheikh's attribution of the account of the man at Uhud
options: reproduce the attribution exactly as the Sheikh gives it and flag the difficulty
correct the narrator to al-Bara ibn ʿAzib
drop the narrator and keep only 'in the two Sahihs'
flags.note: POSSIBLE MISATTRIBUTION — RECORDED, NOT CORRECTED. The account of the man who asked at Uhud whether to fight or to submit, and of whom the Prophet said 'he worked little and was rewarded much', is the well-known report of al-Bara ibn ʿAzib. The Sheikh names Abu Musa. This may be a slip of the tongue in the spoken original, a transcription error, or a reference to a different transmission. The house rule is explicit that an apparent error in the source is translated and flagged, never silently fixed, so his attribution stands exactly as he gives it. The Sheikh's office should resolve it before publication, since an attribution error in a hadith citation is precisely the kind of defect that will be seized on.

flags.arabic: كثير من صفات الله تعالى إنما جاءت في أخبار الآحاد فلا يجب على العوام تعلمها
flags.context: the Sheikh's ruling on what the laity must learn of the divine attributes
options: render literally, as a ruling about obligation to learn, not about the truth of the reports
render as a ruling on the evidentiary standing of singly transmitted reports in creed
render with the theological implication drawn out
flags.note: EDITORIAL REVIEW, AND A DISTINCTION THAT MUST SURVIVE. The Sheikh says that learning these attributes is not OBLIGATORY on the common people, because they come by singly transmitted (āḥād) report. He does not say that such reports are not to be believed, nor that they do not establish creed — which is a separate and fiercely contested question between the theological schools. An English rendering that let the second claim appear would put him in the middle of a controversy he is not entering here. He is answering a pedagogical question about what a layman must be taught. Translated faithfully; the publication decision belongs to Ummah Collective and the Sheikh's office.

flags.arabic: أقاتل أو أسلم؟ فقال: أسلم ثم قاتل
options: shall I fight, or shall I submit? — Submit, then fight
shall I fight, or shall I become a Muslim? — Become a Muslim, then fight
shall I fight, or shall I enter Islam? — Enter Islam, then fight
flags.note: The Arabic verb aslama is the same word in both the question and the answer, and the whole point of the exchange is the ordering: faith before action. 'Submit' keeps the single verb and the ordering; options 2 and 3 read more naturally to an English reader but break the verbal echo the anecdote turns on. A reviewer should decide, as the choice will recur across the corpus.

options: the divine decree (al-qadar), its good and its evil
destiny, both its good and its bad
God's determination, the good of it and the evil of it
flags.note: qadar is on the style guide's list of terms pending a fixed rendering (§13). The identical clause appears in records 561 and 563 of this slice, and the same rendering must be applied to all three once it is fixed.

Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

The source writes the eulogy after the Prophet's name sometimes in full and sometimes as the abbreviation (ص). Both are rendered as 'peace and blessings be upon him'; the source form is preserved in body_ar.

There is no question in the body; the question is in the title alone, and the body opens directly with the answer, whose 'it' refers back to the title's 'creed'. The site must render title and body together.
The title's verb nufahhim is causative — 'make understand' — and has been rendered 'teach'; al-ṣighār, literally 'the little ones', is rendered 'children'.
The Sheikh gives the exchange at Uhud in his own words rather than as a quotation, and marks only the Prophet's closing sentence as quoted; the English follows that.
'Singly transmitted reports' for āḥād follows the glossary entry for the term.
